description: Run Salesforce REST composite resources under /services/data/v{version}/composite on the registered org. Operations: composite (POST /composite; body compositeRequest of up to 25 subrequests with referenceId, allOrNone, collateSubrequests), graph (POST /composite/graph; body graphs), batch (POST /composite/batch; body batchRequests, haltOnError), tree (POST /composite/tree/{sobject}; body records with attributes.referenceId), collections_create (POST /composite/sobjects; body records, allOrNone), collections_retrieve (GET /composite/sobjects/{sobject}; query ids and fields, up to 200 ids), collections_retrieve_many (POST /composite/sobjects/{sobject}; body ids and fields), collections_update (PATCH /composite/sobjects; body records), collections_upsert (PATCH /composite/sobjects/{sobject}/{external_id_field}; body records) and collections_delete (DELETE /composite/sobjects; query ids, allOrNone). Platform Events can be published in bulk with collections_create on an __e type. Optional headers pass documented request headers such as Sforce-Call-Options. Salesforce permissions alone decide each operation. Returns job_id/status queued.
embedding_description: Bundle many Salesforce record operations in one call with the REST composite, composite graph, batch, sObject tree and sObject Collections resources: create, read, update, upsert and delete up to 200 records, or chain dependent subrequests by reference id. Writes and deletes are first-class; org permissions decide.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Queued dispatch: job_id and status. Completion: family, operation, method, status (HTTP), selected headers, body (compositeResponse, graphs, batch results, tree results or the Collections SaveResult array), correlation_id, error_code for a 4xx/5xx or unknown status, and failures: the count of failed subrequests, graphs or records inside a 2xx response. Credential values are redacted in raw, percent-encoded and base64 forms.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: This operation may have created, changed or deleted records. Queued means the job was accepted, not that Salesforce applied it. A 200 can still carry failed parts: report failures and each failed part's errors. Report deletes from the vendor results, never from job completion alone, and never retry a write automatically.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Run Salesforce composite and sObject Collections requests with the registered user's permissions.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: sf.invalid_params is raised before any vendor call when the operation, sobject or external_id_field API name, record ids, documented query parameter names (ids, fields, allOrNone) or required body members (compositeRequest, graphs, batchRequests, records, ids and fields) do not match the vendor shape. Vendor HTTP errors are completion data with error_code: sf.bad_request (400), sf.session_expired or sf.auth_failed (401), sf.permission_denied (403 INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS), sf.rate_limited (REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED), sf.not_found (404), sf.conflict (409), sf.precondition_failed (412), sf.api_error otherwise.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Read the status, body and failures before retrying. A permission error means the registered user lacks the object or field permission in Salesforce; the plugin adds no gate of its own. Set allOrNone true to roll back every part when one fails. After a transport error read the records first instead of repeating a write.
